# ConR package


<br/><br/>

The ``ConR`` package aims at assisting the preliminary assessment of species
conservation status based on the International Union for Conservation of Nature
(IUCN) Red List Categories and Criteria. More specifically, it helps users to
calculate the population metrics related to the IUCN criteria A, B, C and D and
to assign one of the IUCN categories (i.e. EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD). It
was developed speed up the assessment of hundreds to thousands of species at the
same time.


The ideas behind this package, and its testing involved many people and
institutes.

<!-- See the original paper published in [Ecology and Evolution](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.3704). -->

The package it not available anymore on CRAN because of the recent retirement of various packages (rgdal, rgeos).
The new version is nevertheless available on github and will soon be available on CRAN.

To install the github version :

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("gdauby/ConR")
```


## Install R, ConR and dependent packages

**First step**. Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/).

## Loading ConR


**Attach ConR package**
This should be done everytime you open an R session.

```{r attach, message = FALSE}
library(ConR)
```

**Help files**
Any function in R is documented by a help file which can be obtained by the
following code:

```{r help, eval = FALSE}
?EOO.computing
?AOO.computing
?subpop.comp
?locations.comp
?criterion_A
?EOO.sensitivity
```

A mode detailed manual on how to use this package is available [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gdauby/ConR/devel/vignettes/articles/ConR.pdf).


## A quick example

Occurrence data are given as a `data.frame` whose first three columns are, in
this order, latitude, longitude and taxon name. Column names do not matter, but
their positions do. The package ships a small example dataset:

```{r example-data}
data(dataset.ex)
MyData <- dataset.ex[!dataset.ex$tax %in% c("species_1", "species_2"), ]
MyData$tax <- as.character(MyData$tax)
str(MyData)
```

The extent of occurrence (EOO, in km<sup>2</sup>) is computed for every taxon at
once:

```{r example-eoo}
EOO.computing(MyData, show_progress = FALSE)
```

So is the area of occupancy (AOO, in km<sup>2</sup>), here on the 2 km grid
recommended by IUCN:

```{r example-aoo}
AOO.computing(MyData, show_progress = FALSE)
```

And the number of subpopulations, using a 5 km circular buffer around each
occurrence:

```{r example-subpop}
subpop.comp(MyData, resol_sub_pop = 5, show_progress = FALSE)
```

These metrics, along with the number of locations, feed the assessment functions
`criterion_A()`, `criterion_B()`, `criterion_C()` and `criterion_D()`. See the
manual linked above for the full workflow.
